answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks using transitive trust networks structured across an attestation trellis. Identities are verified via bounded trust flows from seed nodes, confining Sybils behind sparse graph cuts. While an adversary can cheaply draft a sonnet, securing trust edges forces them to lock up verifiable capital and bear counterparty risk per identity. However, sparse connectivity across a karst topology creates artificial bottlenecks that isolate honest peripheral agents.
